stayed here while starting a new job in charlotte. the location is excellent for anything in the university research park/uncc area, or even concord mills or the speedway. i stayed in a "studio suite," which is a bit of a misnomer because it is just a slightly bigger than normal hotel room with a mini-fridge, a single-cup coffeemaker, a tiny microwave, and a couple paper plates. that is the "kitchenette." the good: the room was big and quiet. it had a 37" hd tv. the bed was the best part of the whole thing, it was an extremely soft and yet comfortable king. great sheets, fluffy pillows, well done all around. the hotel decor was sharp, especially in the common areas. the complimentary breakfast did have a couple of hot features (eggs, some sort of meat, biscuits) in addition to the usual cold cereals, juice, muffins, etc. the staff was incredibly friendly and accomodating. the bad: the internet was so slow as to be almost worthless--their complimentary ibahn "high-speed" internet never broke 50kbytes/sec upload or download. wired or wireless, day or night, weekday or weekend, it did not matter. (not a good thing for a hotel in a high-tech business park.) the working desk is right next to the underwindow a/c unit so if you are using it, you are going to freeze your left arm off. the tv cannot be seen from the sofa, only from the bed. as mentioned above, the "kitchenette" is not even worth the term. my second night in the hotel, housekeeping never even entered the bathroom to do anything--so the trash was not thrown out and the towels were not changed. the elevators and hallways, for some odd reason, were always about 90 degrees and muggy even when it was not terribly hot outside. the "fitness center" is two treadmills and a stairclimber, and the indoor pool is very small. as long as you do not need to actually work on the internet, and somebody else is footing the $105+ a night bill, this is not a bad hotel. but in terms of value for money, it is not very good.

you may think it looks out of place, and it certainly does amongst the gothic city - but this classical reconstruction of the parthenon stands out and is really something special.

it's no wonder they call edinburgh the 'athens of the north'.

expensive for the kind of place it is. several issues here that you may want to be aware of. during my first 3 night stay here, night 1 went by just okay as i was exhausted after work and checked in late. night 2, coming back from work..i noticed the room tv turn on and off by itself, as much as once every 2 minutes. called the front desk and they were helpful to change my tv. 30 mins after it started happening again and this time they changed the satallite receiver box. once again it started turning on and off when i called the hotel staff and they gladly put me in another room 1/3 the size of my original room. was the old room inhabited already? the hotel only told me that this place was a 1880 property and anything could be possible. night 3, some serious rumbling and cutting noises in the walls. called the front desk and they said someone was taking kickboxing classes and would pack up soon. bedcovers removed to sleep..noticed it spread out on the used bed as is and the bed not even made up! shocking!! this place is unacceptable. i must also mention the location. not suitable for the faint of heart. the place is flooded with homeless right outside the door and you would see them for as far as your vision would go. cant think of taking late evening walks outside. however, the only single positive experience i had here is the good quality breakfast. without a doubt, this was good breakfast that most hotels may not offer free.

i love the location of this hotel. it is on the river, but in a quiet area about half a mile from the downtown section of the river walk and a mile from the pearl brewery complex and the san antonio museum of art. it is a nice walk in either direction, or you can hop on one of the rio taxis that run along the river on a regular schedule. this hotel is beautiful. it is on the national register of historic places and maintains much of it is historic character and charm. i loved the wooden staircase and the beautiful wood floors. for an older building, the rooms were a nice size. we had a queen suite, which also had a small seating area, and there was more than enough room for the two of us. the bed was comfy and the ceiling fan would be especially nice during hot san antonio summers. i also really liked the fully stocked smeg refrigerator in the room, in lieu of a typical hotel minibar. free and easy to access wifi was also a very nice and welcome touch in an era when many hotels still charge something outrageous for it. since this is an older building, it does have some drawbacks that are inherent with such a structure. the floors creak. you can hear people walking along the hallways outside the room and on the floor above. the rooms are not well-insulated. we could hear every word of the conversation the couple in the room next to ours was having. (every word. not good.) the rooms do not have closets, or even wardrobes. there are hangers in one of the drawers, and a pretty, but not really functional hanger thing on the wall behind the door. the bathrooms are very small, and in ours the antique mirror over the sink was so "antique" that it was not really useable. all of that being said, i would probably stay here again because i loved the hotel's bar/restaurant - ocho. it consists of a basement level bar and a lovely upstairs lounge area with outdoor seating overlooking the river. we spent much of the afternoon out there enjoying our drinks and some wonderful chorizo con queso. after wandering around the river walk for the evening, we even came back to ocho for more drinks and dinner. the service is good, very attentive, and efficient, and the food is excellent. even if i were not staying at the hotel, i would come hang out at ocho. i would probably give this hotel 3.5 "stars" due to the noise issues in the rooms, but i love everything else, so bumped it up to 4.

huge improvement from the old property but it almost seems like they ran out of money right before they finished.

the parking garage is ancient and terribly designed. when you arrive make sure you say that you are a hotel guest (even if you are not) and do not pay the $5 they collect. there are two elevators in the garage but only one has been working since they re-opened in late august. how do they let one elevator stay broken for three months? that single elevator is painfully slow so if you are not carrying much, just walk the stairs though it is not the cleanest or safest feeling but it will save you 5 minutes, seriously. if you check out on a sunday morning when many people are leaving you will wait 10-15 minutes for that single elevator to make the round trip as the line backs up since fewer people can get in the elevator with their bags. this is where you see how terribly slow the elevator is. even though the garage is only 5 levels, it literally takes 3-4 minutes to complete a round trip. 

another thing you will find through the elevators in the garage and both hotel towers is that about 20% of the button lights do not work. you will see people pressing it over and over because the light does not come on. a very very simple and low cost fix but again they neglect this.

no ice machines on the hotel floors. they plan to have an ice machine on every 3rd floor but they were supposed to be in months ago and continue to ignore this issue. will room service bring a bucket of ice to you? yes but wait about 30 minutes and pay a $2 charge plus gratuity. otherwise you can get your ice bucket from your room and bring it down to the casino bar. now think about this for a moment. you generally have to make two round trips to get your ice. go up to your room to get your bucket, come back down to the casino floor to fill it, then go back up to your room. i suggested that each bar carry a large supply of plastic bags so that hotel guests can simply stop by the bar and get their ice without having to make the extra round trip to get their bucket and bag. this solution would be low cost and alleviate much of the frustration but have they done it? of course not. i could also mention that having just one ice machine on every 3 floors is insufficient but it beats having none so we will fight that battle when we get to it.

there are no hair dryers in the room which my wife likes to have. she calls to have one sent to the room, it does not work. calls for another one which also does not work. finally she goes to walgreens and buys her own.

i have clearly focused on the negatives here because i want the plaza to succeed and these are easy fixes. i am hopeful that if enough of us complain, they eventually have to listen and do something about it. please show your support of these issues at the plaza facebook page:
 
aside from that, the rooms are nice and certainly a good value. if they can fix a few of these issues it will be a great value.

i love arizona's beer culture. az has numerous amazing craft breweries and papago is on top of the list for me. 

they are probably best known for their orange blossom. it is a delicious vanilla orange wheat beer that just hits the spot. it is so smooth and full of flavor. their coconut joe has a hint of coconut with strong coffee flavor. they used to have another stout that was irish cream base and i am very sad to report they no longer offer it.

they offer a good variety of draft beers from other craft breweries (local and non) and they have multiple fridges stocked with cold, delicious beer you can purchase and drink right there. 

inside is spacious and has lots of table options. service can be slow but only during peak time and even then, you will not go long without another cold one in your hand.

the food is actually delicious. i am a huge fan of their caprese flat bread. the balsamic reduction is so good! their pizzas are a good size for the price and always consistent in quality and taste. 

they now have the steel growlers, along with their glass, so be sure to pick one up too. the steel growler is the coolest steel ones i have seen so far in local breweries.

outback opened this location up in the mid-90s. the fact that me and my family have never stopped going back should say something.

outback is, essentially, an american restaurant with an australian theme - mostly represented by the names of items on the menu and pictures/items on the wall. pretty much any standard american dine-in restaurant fare you can find here, but they have a few other surprised on the menu as well.

the atmosphere in here can get a bit crowded and noisy at times, but that is to be expected of a place like this. wait times can be frustratingly long during peak hours - even calling ahead does not help much. fortunately, outside the restaurant there are plenty of benches on which to wait, so you will not be left standing. 

the staff are extremely friendly and courteous - these people really go above and beyond what i see at most restaurants of the type. they are good about taking requests if you want an item done a particular way, and are very good about correcting any mistakes they may have made. one night, we were in the restaurant and they were packaging up our leftovers (which we were just taking home to give to the dogs anyway), but they accidentally threw them out. before long, a manager was at our table apologizing, and even gave us a free dessert as a way of making it up to us.

the food itself is some of the best this reviewer has ever had. there is a little bit of everything, and none of it bad. the potato soup here is to die for, easily some of the best i have ever had. the entrees fare just as well - try the victoria's filet with a horseradish crush, and you will see what i mean. 

the long wait times to get into the restaurant during peak hours and the fact that this location is not open for lunch are my only real complaints. if you want a dine-in restaurant with great food, look no further than outback.

i stayed here for a week on business. i gave this hotel an average rating because it is not poor, it is just below average. i booked a superior room. upon arrival my room was freezing. the window ac (yes, window ac) was being held in place with clear, postage tape and was letting a draft in. i put a washcloth in the gap to keep the air out, then 10 min later realized at $300 a night, this was not acceptable. i asked to change rooms. front desk was very friendly and gave me another room. note: not all rooms have window ac. specify if you want a room with central ac/heating. the rooms are small, even by ny standards. and my room was dirty. i found m&m's on the floor and the bathroom tile was pretty dingy and had some calcium and mold buildup. absolutely no counter space in the bathroom. and the blow dryer seemed as if it was ready to give out. the shower water take four minutes to heat up (yes, i timed it). the construction outside started promptly at 7am and i had a screaming kid and barking dog on my floor. the second floor wreaks of cigarette smoke, so if you are sensitive like me..do not stay on the second floor. the fitness center is on the second floor and i would hold my breath from the elevator to the fitness center as the smell was that strong. the elevators are slow. luckily i was on the fourth floor so i took the stairs most of the time. the location is convenient and it seems as if a lot of tourists use this hotel. it was busier than i like for business stays. this hotel is also across the street from a fire station. while i did not hear the sirens, the fire trucks would still come and go creating traffic jams on 77th. the hotel is also next to a parking garage so this area has a lot of traffic. and, this hotel does not offer free wifi. the lobby is nice, but the rooms need attention. for the price and facilities, there are many other options in the area that will get you more for your money. i will not be staying here again.

i *thought* i knew italian food. i thought i had pizza and pasta figured out.

i was wrong.

thanks to my dinner at scarpetta, my appreciation for the sophistication of italian cuisine is vastly more than it used to be.

in other words, scarpetta gave me an education in fine italian dining that i will never forget.

it all happened on a sunday night, which was the only night of the week when i could secure a table at scarpetta -- a restaurant notorious for its difficulty in scoring a reservation. after walking through the narrow entrance hall on the third floor of the cosmopolitan hotel, i was greeted by a spacious and elegantly appointed dining room. i was lucky enough to have a window seat directly overlooking the bellagio fountains.

i quickly received a menu from my kind and gracious server, giampaolo, and found myself drooling over its mouthwatering options. while i waited, giampaolo brought by a breadbasket with sides of citrus-inflused olive oil, eggplant tapanade, and whipped mascarpone cheese. the breadbasket was superb -- especially the stromboli with cheese and succulent salami baked inside.

i was not in the mood for wine, so i started by ordering of their signature cocktails -- a st. germain/prosecco spritzer. sweet and refreshing, it was a lovely start to dinner.

for an appetizer, i had the yellowtail crudo. the raw fish was extremely fresh and beautifully seasoned. i especially enjoyed that little punch of sea salt that hits you after the rest of the fish is gone. (who said that japanese restaurants have a monopoly on raw fish?)

the real show-stopper was the entree -- duck and foie gras ravioli. i do not claim to be a foie gras expert, but this dish was revelatory. the ravioli dough was delicate and flavorful. the duck and foie gras filling could only be described as pure decadence. the sauce drizzled on top provided a beautiful contrast. this was one of the top dishes that i have ordered in any restaurant -- ever.

after the ravioli, i was too full to order dessert, but giampaolo was still kind enough to bring over two complementary petit fours -- a cinnamon biscotti cookie and a chocolate truffle. both were outstanding.

everything about scarpetta is outstanding -- from the service, to the ambiance, to the extraordinary food. 

if i could, i would get my culinary education here every day.

ok, i am going to depart from the pack here a little..yes, this hotel is dated, and yes, it is got some issues with carpet needing cleaning and the like. however, it also gets extra points for a few amenities you often do not find in hotels with price tags twice this high. i stayed here twice - on both ends of a scuba diving liveaboard trip out to see some great white sharks, long story - and my review applies to both rooms. as i have mentioned in other reviews, certain things usually score extra credit points from me: good ventilation and water pressure, a comfy bed, a quiet room, and access to snacks and soft drinks. this place scored high on all those counts, honestly. air conditioning worked great, the rooms were comfortable, the bathrooms had recently been remodeled and were quite spacious. one room was just average size, but one was huge! this place actually is something of a flophouse for several companies that run trips out to see the sharks, and some outfits that do sportfishing, so you may want to call ahead to double check room availability. i screwed up my travel plans, then called at 8 am to book a room for an extra night and it turned out to have been a great thing..i heard later the place filled up shortly thereafter. a couple of real extra credit points to this hotel: there was a fridge and a microwave in each room; the drink and snack machines were amply stocked, not broken, and conveniently located in the lobby - and, oh joy! a change machine! best of all, this hotel was silent as the grave. i stayed up super late one night and was not awakened early the next morning by loud talking, slamming doors, any of that nonsense. also, there is plenty of parking, and the hotel is located very near some really wonderful restaurants (we liked the fish grotto and, aw heck, another one the name of which escapes me right now..but seriously, there are several outstanding joints within easy walking distance. there is also a denny's a block away and i had no trouble ordering a pizza late one night.) the neighborhood was just fine, not frightening, and you are within sight of the incredibly beautiful harbor. you are also right on top of the airport, and yet somehow not within the flight path..i did not hear much jet noise. the internet worked great!! this one gets real points from me..i have stayed in "luxury" hotels where the wireless signal was terrible, or they charged $30 per night or something absurd. at the ramada, i got a strong, clear signal, no trouble logging on, and no need for a "bridge" for rent from the front desk or similar foolishness. i would stay here again in a hot second. i think the value is actually pretty good for the price paid. my only real complaint was with the tiny elevator - i had to rearrange my bags a few times to get them onto the cart so it all would fit..

we chose this hotel for its location, services and rating on ta. all expectations were met but for a couple of issues. booked on their web site for a great rate, when i called the hotel to make an adjustment to the booking they actually found me a lower rate with more perks. great! somehow those perks did not make it to the front desk and i had to remind them of the picnic and late check-out included in our rate. they made it happen with no issues, but i had to have the charge removed at check out, because again, they did not enter it correctly into their system. to be sure the front desk happily took care of all the issues, but it would be best to not have to double check every detail. beautiful room with an amazing view of the hancock tower. in room service was spectacular. we both found the bed to be too soft for comfortable sleeping. i got used to it, but my wife never did. this will probably have us looking for a different place to stay next time. another irksome quirk that i cannot blame on the hotel is that we had virtually no service from at&t in our room on the 21st floor. i cannot understand it as the hotel is not surrounded by huge stone buildings to block reception. it was just another unfortunate negative of our stay. lastly i am always offended to stay at a hotel of this caliber and be charged for in room internet access. i know most hotels charge for this service, but really, what year is this? a better hotel should offer this as part of its services. to sum up, this is a very nice hotel with an amazing location. some people will find the beds to be like sleeping in a cloud. those people will love their experience. if you need more support you might want to check with the front desk and see if they can accommodate you. the staff was always happy to help and made any issues disappear quickly.

sauce is my absolute fav. i do not think i have had a single thing there that i have not liked. while they are pretty well known for their pizza which is absolutely delish, i usually tend to eat a little on the healthier side and get either the turkey and feta salad or this other salad that has pears in it (i kind of forget exactly what it is, but i have gotten it a few times). i also like the soup and you cannot go wrong with their turkey sandwich either. oh, and their mac n cheese!! so delish. those are pretty good standbys, and it is nice that they give you bread and butter on the side no matter what you order, even if you do get a sandwich which a lot of places tend to skimp on the bread if you ordered bread as a staple of your meal (which is probably better for you anyway, but thanks for the extra bread, sauce!) it is also nice that it is really close to a lot of stuff, so it is a good lunch spot during the work day. do not get caught browsing at urban outfitters while you wait for your food though or you might get stuck spending 100 bucks in about 5 minutes like i did last time i went. yikes.

this hotel is right behind the john hancock center, and a block away from water tower place where the new american girl store is, so it cannot be beat location wise if those are on your list. we booked a king suite, our gold hhonors status got us a free 'upgrade', to a lake view room on the 27th floor. if you are considering paying extra for one of these rooms, do not. the view is mainly of several residential towers, and we could see what one guy was grilling on his balcony at one point. the room itself was clean, but the wear is starting to show. yellowing switch plates, peeling wall paper, toothpaste stains on the mirror frame etc. the 'king' bed (we have one at home, this was not a king size bed) was comfortable, and we slept well. the sofa sleeper was pretty lumpy and i doubt an adult would be comfortable, but our kids were ok with it. the staff were however quick to respond when we found our safe had not been left unlocked by the previous guest, and when we needed a new hair dryer because the old one was broken. we did not eat here, the prices for breakfast were a little ridiculous ($14 for a coffee and a danish?!). we also did not park here because $55 per day is frankly extortionate, the john hancock building where oprah lives charges less. next time we are staying in chicago i will pay the extra $25 and stay at the conrad.

my mom and i booked a room here for the weekend of a family gathering and to see a show at the curran theatre. the hotel makes a great effort to add charm and warmth to an already-welcoming space; the lobby is filled with comfortable chairs in small groups and low tables featuring classic card & board games. some here have mentioned the well-attended wine tastings in the evening, but there is also a nice coffee service in the morning. when we returned to our hotel after the play, people were still relaxing around the fireplace with a glass of wine, playing cards. the secret, i think, to this homey feel is the extraordinarily friendly service. everyone we interacted with at the hotel was helpful and engaging. the room was not huge, but it was much bigger than i had been led to expect from the reviews here - in fact, the room featured a well-sized bathtub. the only complaint i have is that they charge for computer access in the much-publicized business center. for a hotel in this price range, with keycode access to the biz center, it seems insulting to tack on a usage and printing charge. overall, though, great stay!

being a fully raw foodie, i must say i do enjoy coming here for brunch. we have been here a few times and we have not been disappointed.as i enjoy raw living food it is great to take friends and family to ashleys, who are not necessarily raw as they can select their selection of breakfast from poached eggs,scrambled with smoked salmon etc. my husband absolutely loves the morning breakfast there where he tends to have his smoked salmon, poached eggs, sprouted baked beans (and i must say it might sound strange but boy it tastes 100 times better than that nasty canned stuff) and a light toasted bread. plus it is also not drenched in oil when you order a fried egg or scrambled eggs, it tastes clean on the pallet.there is also healthy granola to choose from, although it is not fully raw as it contains oats, it is very tasty.i tend to have the raw food dishes they have on the menu and all of them are superb, although i would have liked to have seen more raw living options on the menu to select from. but other than that i can go there anytime! perhaps a rawfood pizza! all the juices and smoothies are also made from scratch and there is also no preservatives or sugars added, this is the way fresh juices and smoothies should be served! you can also have your selection of milks, for example almond milk, soy milk or just the normal cow's milkall the sauces on the raw food dishes are also living raw sauces, made only from soaked nuts then blended to create a "raw living cheese sauce", there is also a natural raw salsa! they also serve this water that has health properties and has a perfect ph balance that enhances the bodies natural healing properties and promotes good health.the only down side to my times visited there is the fact that some of the waiters do not seem to mention these things to you.the water was just put down on our table, so upon receiving it i saw the sticker on the bottle and then googled it, then only i learnt what the water is about.i also found when my husband ordered his version of an english breakfast i asked instead of giving my husband cheese could he rather have the raw nut cheese, the waiter seemed a bit confused and in then end when my husband got his dish there was no raw living cheese, only the normal parmesan cheese. so that was a bit disappointing as i feel this is a unique selling point of having some raw food options on the menu and also educating and making the customers excited about the experience in eating the healthy food at ashely's, as i think this is what the whole concept is behind ashley's living food.

my family and i stayed here a week ago and personally, i was rather disappointed. ok, so first of all, the staff were a little hostile from time to time but concierge was helpful. before i go on to the room we had, i would just like to say that the pool was not as big as it seems on the website, and also you have to pay to use the business center as they only have free wifi in the lobby.. anyway, we stayed in a double double junior suite on the fifteenth floor. it was dusty, and either the sofas or the ac was letting off a stale, unpleasant smell. when we returned from a long day out, the beds never seemed made, as there were lumps and bumps everywhere on the duvet, and for the size of the beds, the pillows were small and uncomfortable. it was difficult to figure out how to access the normal channels on tv, as you would try and be tricked into watching a harmless movie (when in reality, you would have to pay). at times, i felt as if the everything had a cost.. they put two bottles of complimentary water in the bathroom (strange place to put them..?!) and then put two in the actual room. the two in the room had labels round their necks stating that they were water but in very small letters read '$4.00'. i was shocked. also, the bathroom was small, but at least it was well equipped. the mirror was found in the impractical place of behind the bathroom door. there was only one small wardrobe for all four of us to share, which was a bit of a pain, so i had to fold all of my clothes and bundle them into drawers. on the contrary, the view was wonderful. we managed to see a beautiful part of boston and cambridge, across the charles river. also, the location was good, as the hotel was attached to copley place mall via a covered bridge, and whilst walking to that mall, you would pass a conveniently positioned starbucks, from where we bought breakfast and snacks. once you reached copley place mall, you could walk straight through, then across another covered bridge, to the prudential center, stocked with shops and a food court. we came to the prudential center very often to eat and shop. some mentionable places to eat are the cheesecake factory, p.f. changs, anywhere in the food court and just past the cheesecake factory was the cold stone cremery- try their ice cream sundaes! overall, the hotel was conveniently located but not all that it was made out to be.

this is the perfect example of how misleading photos and descriptions can be, at times. i was under the impression that the hotel was entirely renovated and, as this is not a heritage or historical building, i was expecting new furniture, fixtures, technology etc. unfortunately, i have found this not to be true, however, the hotel sensibly uses the wording ''redesigned and refreshed'' on its website. this translates into the following: - there is still old furniture in the rooms ( for instance, in my room there was a very used and scratched coffee table - i am sure, of no historical value) - a very tired looking velvet couch - a flat tv set (lg), hardly new generation, although i am not an expert, however, most other mandarin oriental hotels have state of the art bang & olufsen tv sets - air-conditioning has been untouched - probably as old as the building (25 years), has not automatic setting and quite noisy (a disturbing humming, even when set on low speed) - wall tiling of the bathroom does not match the rest of the design - there is still an old, wobbling lamp, which again seems out of decor as for the new stuff, it is definitely a matter of personal taste - to me, most of it seemed of rather basic quality, for instance the new business desk chair is covered in a plastic material, definitely not leather. this is also the first mandarin oriental i stay at, which does not have predominantly natural bathroom amenities - it features molton brown. the arrival experience is also in sharp contrast with other mandarin oriental hotels - a lackluster lobby, connected to the only restaurant of the hotel, hence the smell of food (i was unfortunate to check in at lunch time). service is of a good five star standard, being consistent throughout all departments.

schizophrenic but promising. 
as with any new restaurant, bugs to be worked out. the downstairs check-in/bar wait area appears really disorganized, probably more so than it is. the huge entry seems to be a huge waste of space, especially when you see how cramped some of the areas upstairs are. the butcher area is cool, but i need to see if the selection and quality are up to the hype. 

my biggest issue was with the menu. it is poorly laid out at best. they claim to feature their small plates and "butcher cuts", yet they are some of the smaller sections on the menu, compared to salads? and lunches??
also, the pitch the waiter gives about the specialty cuts being so unique-tri tip, sirloin, flank steak??
having said all that, the food was good, some of it very good. the sides were terrific (cauliflower, kale, bone marrow,asparagus, etc). the hangar steak is terrific. 
however, they also offer 3 cuts "by the inch"-ny strip, ribeye, filet. the "inch" was more like a half and the meat was ok. just ok. tender but not that flavorful and disappointing. 
one great thing-bring your own wine-no corkage fee. 

as soon as this place decides what it really wants to be, it will improve dramatically. i would love to think they would move away from trying to be all things and really emphasize the small plates and specialty cuts. vegas, and the neighborhood, needs what echo and rig could be.

located in the encore, botero, named after the colombian artist fernando botero, houses much of his beautiful artwork, complete with a sculpture of a voluptuous woman in the middle of the restaurant. we luckily got a great table right by the statute and facing the grand encore beach club pool. 

we trekked all the way from the golden nugget (we went to see one of gallagher's last watermelon smashing shows), so we were starving and were going for any appetizers. i got the petite filet, 8 ounces, with the chimichurri preparation. the bf got the bone-in ribeye which came with a trio of sauces. the filet was cooked perfectly, but i did not care for the chimichurri sauce. the sauce was not flavorful at all, it was more of a dry-rub. i have had better chimichurri at a backyard bbq. the bf's ribeye was much tastier than my filet and the three sauces were an interesting touch. for our side, we got the truffle mac and cheese, which was good, but not as decedent as i expected. 

the ambience and of course, my company, was amazing. however, for being the encore, i was just not impressed. it is definitely not something to write home to mom about.

sydney - amsterdam - frankfurt -singapore (stopover) - sydney. all flights were up to the 'old' sia standards of service. check-ins and transfers were easy and the lounges were clean and well-stocked. meals ordered online and were tasty and well presented with plentiful beer, wines and spirits offered with them and during the flight - possible a little too enthusiastically. the cabin crew were friendly and efficient and made the flights very pleasant indeed. you do need to ask for amenity kits and slippers if you want them and the absence of an offer of hot towels was initially disappointing but a plentiful supply was discovered in the wash rooms for self-serve. the lie-flat beds were made up by the crew if you showed any hesitation in figuring out how they worked and were comfortable once you became used to the idea of sleeping on a bed where the lower half was offset to the upper half. cabin wifi worked ok and the ife seemed to have a reasonable selection, although eating and sleeping were my preferred options on the overnight flights. all in all, sia seems to be back with their reputation intact.
